top_stories.title: GRP Arakkonam arrest head constable on sexual harassment charge - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Sheikh Abdullah**, a 42-year-old head constable from Coimbatore, was arrested by **Government Railway Police (GRP)** in Arakkonam for alleged sexual harassment of a law student on a train. The incident occurred on December 20, 2025, when the suspect was returning to Coimbatore from Chennai.  The woman passenger filmed the incident and it went viral online, leading to public outrage. Abdullah's bail petition before the Supreme Court was rejected recently.

top_stories.title: Separate ELEVATE track for Beyond Bengaluru startups welcomed - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The State government's** recent decision to introduce a separate ELEVATE track for startups outside the Bengaluru region has been welcomed by **Karnataka Digital Economy Mission’s (KDEM)** Mysuru cluster head Sudheer Shankar.  He stated that this change will address concerns about unfair competition between startups in tier 2 and tier 3 regions and Bengaluru-based startups, as **ELEVATE** previously provided grants to startups in all regions of the state.

top_stories.title: Global Travel Market 2026 in Kerala clocks over 60,000 B2B meets - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Global Travel Market (GTM 2026)** concluded in Thiruvananthapuram, with over 60,000 B2B meetings facilitated. The three-day event saw participation from **domestic and international buyers**, including **2,000 domestic buyers** and **100 international buyers**.  The exhibition featured stalls representing leading tourism and hospitality stakeholders from across India, organized by **South Kerala Hoteliers Forum (SKHF)**, **Thiruvananthapuram Chamber of Commerce and Industries (TCCI)**, **Thavass Ventures**, and **Metro Mart**, in association with **Kerala Tourism** and **India Tourism**.

top_stories.title: Tipra Motha MLA criticises Pradyot over Pushpabanta Palace hotel project - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Chitta Ranjan Debbarma**, a **Tipra Motha MLA**, criticized **Pradyot Kishore Manikya**, the party founder, for attending the foundation stone-laying ceremony of a hotel project at the site of Pushpabanta Palace.  Debbarma alleged that **Manikya**, who had previously opposed the government's decision to hand over the palace land to the Taj Group of Hotels, now appears to have changed his stance by participating in the event. The ceremony was attended by **Amit Shah**, **Manik Saha**, **Sushanta Chowdhury**, and **Pradyot Kishore Manikya**.

top_stories.title: If Modi can stop wars, why can’t he stop paper leaks? Cockroach party’s Dipke targets PM | The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Abhijit Dipke**, founder of the **Cockroach Janta Party**, continued his protests demanding the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan**, Union Education Minister, over the NEET paper leak controversy.  He criticized Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** for failing to address the issue and questioned the government's handling of examination leaks. Dipke stated that the party would continue focusing on issues affecting young people across India, but declined to comment on its future as a political entity. He also addressed criticism from BJP leaders and social media users regarding his credentials and alleged anti-government agenda, stating he remains in India and will not return to the United States.

top_stories.title: Penguin India's Rejection of Joe Sacco's Muzaffarnagar Riot Book Matters
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Joe Sacco**, a renowned comics journalist, had his book "The Once and Future Riot" rejected for distribution in **India** by **Penguin India**. The publisher cited technicalities regarding an image on the book's map but this decision raises concerns about censorship and the accessibility of truth-telling in the country.  Sacco's meticulous research involved interviewing people affected by the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots, highlighting the importance of comics journalism for capturing complex narratives and personal experiences within political contexts.

top_stories.title: Cotton sowing area likely to rise by 10-15% this kharif season: Officials | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Maharashtra**'s agriculture department predicts a 10-15% increase in cotton cultivation areas for the 2026-27 kharif season due to higher market demand and better prices. Farmers, particularly in Vidarbha and Marathwada, are shifting back to cotton from soybean after disappointing yields for soybeans this year.  While cotton prices have surged recently, experts warn that these high prices may not translate into guaranteed returns for farmers due to potential quality issues during procurement and lack of a robust support system.

top_stories.title: In a first, Maharashtra minister joins Operation Blue Star anniversary at Damdami Taksal | Chandigarh News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Girish Mahajan**, **Maharashtra**’s Minister for Water Resources, became the first state government representative to attend the Operation Blue Star anniversary commemoration at the headquarters of **Damdami Taksal** in Amritsar.  He addressed the gathering, calling June 6th a “kaala din” and drawing parallels between the violence inflicted on Sikhs after Indira Gandhi's assassination and the invasion of Ahmed Shah Abdali. Mahajan also highlighted Maharashtra’s commitment to Sikh history with programs commemorating Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib and announced new initiatives in Guru Tegh Bahadur’s name. He concluded his address by appealing for help tackling drug abuse among Punjab’s youth.

top_stories.title: How 6.30 am tutorials by ‘market guru’ cost IT professional Rs 4.43 crore in trading fraud | Pune News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: A 46-year-old IT professional was defrauded of Rs 4.43 crore in a two-week span after being lured into a fraudulent WhatsApp group and trading application. The group, posing as a legitimate stock market advisory forum, featured daily tutorials from an administrator named Maira who claimed to be a "market guru".  The victim was persuaded to download the app and create an account, where he saw steadily rising profits that prompted him to transfer large sums of money through multiple transactions.  Authorities are investigating the case and urging citizens to verify trading platforms with SEBI, avoid downloading investment apps from social media links, and report suspected cyber fraud on 1930 or the cybercrime reporting portal.

top_stories.title: Saudi Arabia arrests more than 7,700 residency, labour and border violators in one-week crackdown | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Saudi** authorities conducted nationwide enforcement operations between May 28 and June 3, resulting in the arrest of 7,760 individuals for violations related to residency, labor, and border regulations. The **Ministry of Interior** reported that Ethiopians constituted the majority of those detained at the border (70%), followed by Yemenis (28%).  The operations also involved the deportation of 4,690 individuals and the referral of others to obtain travel documents or complete arrangements for departure. Authorities emphasized that facilitating illegal entry, movement, or sheltering of undocumented individuals is a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment, fines, and property confiscation.
